title: A bill to ensure the security of office space rented by Senators, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
This act establishes certain security-related exceptions to limitations on the size and cost of Senators' home state office space. (The size and cost limitations vary based on the population of the Senator's home state.)

The act specifies that any portion of home state office space that is used for building security or safety measures is not included in calculating the total amount of office space subject to applicable maximum size. The building safety and security measures must be (1) of a kind authorized by the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration and (2) approved by the Senate Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of the Senate.

The act also specifies that an information technology security closet and a secure lobby or reception area are security or safety enhancements that are of a kind authorized by the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration.

The act also excludes the cost of building security and safety measures from the limitation on the cost of renting office space in the home state. Such costs must be (1) of a kind authorized by the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, (2) approved by the Senate Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of the Senate, and (3) itemized separately in a manner approved by the Senate Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of the Senate.

summary.headline: New law lets Senators' home state offices add approved security space and costs without counting them against size and rent limits.
summary.what_it_does: Senators' offices in their home states have limits on how big they can be and how much rent they can cost, based on the state's population. This law says office space used for approved security or safety features does not count toward the size limit, and the cost of those features does not count toward the rent limit. The features must be the kind allowed by the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration and approved by the Senate Sergeant at Arms; costs must also be listed separately. The law names an IT security closet and a secure lobby or reception area as allowed features.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. Senators and their home state office staff
who_it_affects.how: Their state offices can include extra approved security space, such as secure lobbies and IT security closets, beyond the normal size and rent limits.

who_it_affects.group: Senate Sergeant at Arms and Senate Committee on Rules and Administration
who_it_affects.how: They decide which security features qualify and approve the space and costs that are left out of the limits.

who_it_affects.group: Landlords who rent office space to Senators
who_it_affects.how: Leases may include separately listed security costs that are paid outside the usual rent cap.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 26, 2024; the summary does not state a separate effective date.
